note: Mauritius's largest banks are MCB, SBM and Absa Bank (Mauritius); MCB's and Absa's price lists were read, and SBM's wasn't reached. MCB's statement of interest rates and service charges (last updated 7 October 2026), read for every personal credit card: the rate is the prime lending rate of 6.90% plus a margin, 9.50% on the American Express Green and Gold and the VISA Platinum and Signature (16.40% a year) and 13.50% on the MasterCard/VISA Classic and Gold and the MasterCard PRIMO (20.40%); primary cards cost 1,500, 3,000, 1,500, 2,500, 200, 950 and 150 rupees a year before VAT, whose rate the list doesn't state (so it isn't written); a cash advance costs a flat 100 rupees locally (2% abroad, not written); going over the limit costs 200 rupees on the first four and 150 on the rest; conversion is 2.50%. The card the file named before, 'MasterCard/ VISA Classic', is kept with its terms extended; the 'MasterCard/ VISA' cards are written as one card each, as the list prices them. Absa Bank (Mauritius)'s personal tariff guide (effective 1 June 2026): its Platinum, Gold and Classic credit cards cost 1,725, 1,092.50 and 230 rupees a year with VAT, no joining fee, 2.13% a month, 2.10% for a cash advance (at least 150 rupees), 3% forex, 400 rupees for a returned payment, a minimum payment of 5% (at least 2,000, 1,000 and 100 rupees) and up to 52 days interest free; its late and excess-limit fees, each '1% of amount due' (at least 250 and 200 rupees), don't make clear whether the amount due is the minimum or the balance, so they aren't written. Business, corporate and foreign-currency cards aren't written. Wave 4 (30 October 2026), for a third bank: SBM's site answered 503 (an upstream connection timeout) on its cards pages and a search found no SBM Mauritius tariff, so AfrAsia Bank, a large Mauritian bank that publishes its Bank of Mauritius template, was added: its template (last updated 8 June 2026), read for its credit cards: the World, Titanium and Gold cards cost MUR 402.50, 195.50 and 805.00 a month for the primary card, VAT included (the Gold's 'payable upfront'; each is written as the monthly fee the template names), charge 15%, 20% and 24% a year on the balance and on cash advances, 2.5% for a cash advance in Mauritius (at least MUR 100; 2.5%, at least 250, abroad, not written), 3% on payments in another currency, MUR 200 late and MUR 200 over the limit, ask a minimum monthly repayment of 5%, and give up to 48 days interest free when the balance is repaid in full (written at 48). The quasi-cash commission, courier and replacement charges aren't written. BCP Bank's template gives its credit card rate as 'n/a'; MauBank's template (last updated 5 June 2026) also publishes its Visa cards' terms (1.80% a month, annual fees of 230, 920 and 1,380 rupees) but wasn't written, three banks being the aim. So Mauritius has three banks' cards. Wave 5 (2026-10-30), minimum payments: MCB's pages for its Classic, Gold, Mastercard Primo, Visa Platinum and Visa Signature cards offer repayment terms from 5% to 100%, written as 5%, the least. No minimum payment is published for its American Express Green and Gold; tried: their card pages (read 2026-10-30, none stated), its 'your exclusive cards' page (5% to 100% for a pack of three cards it doesn't name, not read as these), its rates and fees (none), and archive.org's API (a snapshot of the Gold page of 4 August 2026; web.archive.org itself is refused by this research's connection).
